submitter: bugs_open/257 Path A — bugfix_257_token_budget_at_the_client lane. Filed by the provocation_pipeline lane 2026-08-12, unowned until today (who-owns.py: one commit, no owning workstream; no live session transcript mentions it).
rationale:
bugs_open/257: the output-token budget has exactly ONE enforced resolution point — ExecuteAIStepAction (ai_actions.go:358-364) — and using it is OPTIONAL. The provider clients read max_tokens only from the per-call options map, so any caller that builds a client itself and calls GenerateText(ctx, prompt, nil) gets the hardcoded 2048 no matter what ai_service.max_tokens says. Nothing states that contract, nothing checks it, and the compiler is happy either way because GenerateText accepts nil.

This is not theoretical. On 2026-08-10 a step was given max_tokens: 8000 by migration 372 and the very next run still died at output_tokens=2048; the config was then changed a SECOND time against a key nothing read (WRONG_CALLS.md). Three things hide it and they compound: the config LOOKS right; the error echoes the OLD number back after you change it; and these calls write no llm_call_log row, because that table is written by the very function being bypassed — so the fleet's own truncation instrument is blind to exactly the calls most likely to truncate.

Four council seats (reuse_agent, constitution, prior_art_librarian, architecture) reached this conclusion independently in round 65d153f0. The architecture seat asked for either a census of direct call sites or moving budget resolution into the client itself. The census was done and recorded; the move was 'owed, not done'. This submission is that move.

WHY THIS CANDIDATE AND NOT THE OTHERS. The bug lists four. Candidate 2 (extract the duplicated precedence rule) ends drift but leaves the contract optional — a future direct caller still reproduces the bug by construction. Candidate 4 (a lint) detects the next occurrence rather than preventing it. Candidate 1 removes the CHOICE: there is no longer a way to call a provider client and miss the configured budget. It is the only one that makes the bad state unrepresentable rather than visible.

BLAST RADIUS — MEASURED, NOT ARGUED (owner ruling 2026-07-28). I enumerated every client construction site rather than reasoning about the common case: grep -rn 'aiservice.(NewClient|NewAnthropicClient|NewGeminiClient|NewOllamaClient)(' --include=*.go, minus tests, returns SEVEN. The claim this change alters ZERO requests in the fleet today rests on them one by one:
  1. ai_actions.go:1398 (canonical, 193 active agents) — createAIClient(ctx, aiServiceConfig) at :287 and the options build at :361 read the SAME merged map, produced once by resolveAIServiceConfig at :243. If the key is present, options carry it and per-call still wins -> identical. If absent, the client default is absent too -> identical. If only agent-level default_config.max_tokens is set (outside the ai_service block, never passed to a constructor), options carry it -> identical. There is no case where the two disagree, because they are one map.
  2. contentcreator/agent.go:123 — config has no max_tokens; options always set it (:720, default 3000). No change.
  3. reasoning/agent.go:71 — config HAS max_tokens (configs/reasoning-agent.yaml: 2048) and options are nil. This is the one site whose behaviour changes: the key becomes live. Its VALUE is 2048, so the request is unchanged.
  4-6. tools-api gripper.go:63 / position.go:77 / defend.go:83 — inline literal configs with no max_tokens; all three pass explicit options. No change.
  7. rag_actions.go:374 — ollama, embeddings only (GenerateEmbedding); no text budget involved.
Live census of what is configured: 193 active non-snapshot agent_definitions; 3 set ai_service.max_tokens (diagnose-agent 32000, feed-triage 4000, site-adoption-agent 16000); 10 set agent-level max_tokens. All 13 go through site 1, hence all 13 are unaffected.

I am deliberately NOT claiming existing config will 'self-heal'. WRONG_CALLS.md:1262 records that exact claim being made from a count and refuted by the query (bugs_open/009 said 17 agents / 10 self-healing; the live query returned 16 and zero). I queried. The answer is that ONE construction site names the key off the canonical path, and its value makes the request identical.

OPT-IN, UNSAFE SIDE DEFAULT-OFF (owner ruling 2026-08-02 §2 / RFC_010; the shape bugs_open/244 shipped into this same client). The new arm fires only when an operator has explicitly put max_tokens in the ai_service block a client is built from. A config that never named it produces a byte-identical request. The opt-in signal is the config key itself, deliberately NOT a second key — the whole defect is that ai_service.max_tokens did not mean what it said, and curing that with a different spelling would leave two keys for one budget.

TELLING THE OTHER CONSUMERS, NOT MERELY MEASURING THEM (owner ruling 2026-07-29 §3). The consumers of this seam are the seven sites above. What changes about their guarantee, stated as a sentence they would care about: 'if your ai_service config names max_tokens, that number now reaches the API even when you pass no options; previously only the options map could set it.' Named in the bug file and the lane PLAN so their owners meet it where they look.

ONE HONEST DIVERGENCE. ai_actions.go:361 reads aiServiceConfig['max_tokens'].(float64) — float64 only. My reader also accepts int, int64 and json.Number, because the SAME key arrives as float64 from jsonb (agent_definitions) and as int from YAML (configs/*.yaml via viper) and a client cannot know which. A config holding an int would therefore start working where it silently did not. That cannot happen from jsonb, so it cannot happen on the canonical path today; it is a change in the correct direction and I state it rather than let it be discovered.

§4's [UNMEASURED] QUESTION, ANSWERED. The filing flagged reasoning-agent as hard-pinned to 2048 but said plainly it had not established whether it truncates, warning that llm_call_log cannot answer it. Measured by the route the filing prescribed — the pod, not the table: 3 replicas Running; their ENTIRE log is startup, zero request-handling lines, zero TruncatedError; and grep -rn 'system.agent.reasoning.requests' finds the consumer plus ONE other hit, a hardcoded 'known topics' list in an admin endpoint. There is no producer in the codebase. So: a deployed service consuming a topic nothing writes to. The defect is real, the burn is zero. I therefore make the key live and LEAVE ITS VALUE AT 2048 — raising a budget with no evidence of truncation is precisely what this bug's §2.2 warns against.

plan.summary: Move output-token budget resolution INTO the three provider clients, from the ai_service config they are already constructed with. New precedence at the wire: options['max_tokens'] (per-call, wins, unchanged) > ai_service.max_tokens from the construction config (NEW) > provider fallback (unchanged: DefaultMaxOutputTokens for anthropic/gemini, no num_predict at all for ollama). Every constructor already receives the whole ai_service map and already reads 'model' out of it with a default fallback — this is one more key from a map already in hand, in the shape that key already uses, not new plumbing. Behaviour-neutral across all seven construction sites today (enumerated in the rationale). Candidate 2 is deliberately out of scope, with reasons, and recorded as follow-up.

edits.rationale: ONE resolver, in the package that owns the wire, so the three providers cannot drift on what counts as a configured budget — the drift this bug's §3 is about. Accepts int, int64, float64 and json.Number because the same key arrives as float64 from jsonb and int from YAML; a float64-only read (what ai_actions.go:361 does) silently drops the YAML path, which is exactly the config reasoning-agent carries. Requires > 0: zero is not 'no budget', it is a 400 from Anthropic, so a typo must read as unset rather than become an outage. Returns (int, bool) so callers can distinguish 'operator chose nothing' from 'operator chose a number' — a distinction an int alone cannot carry, and the reason anthropic (send a floor) and ollama (omit the field) can implement OPPOSITE policies over one answer. DefaultMaxOutputTokens names the 2048 that was previously a literal in two files.

The struct kept apiKey, model, httpClient and DISCARDED the rest of the config it was handed — including max_tokens. Store it at construction exactly as 'model' already is. In generate, the request body's literal 2048 becomes the resolved budget; the existing options override at :294-296 is untouched, so the canonical path is byte-identical. The __sent_max_tokens write-back at :301 reads requestBody['max_tokens'], so llm_call_log.max_tokens follows automatically and does not under-report a config-sourced budget.

INCLUDES THE ZERO-BUDGET FLOOR, which was NOT in the original design and was found by measurement: every fake in this package's tests builds a client as a STRUCT LITERAL, bypassing the constructor, so the new field is the zero value — and `max_tokens: 0` is a 400 (on gemini, 0 becomes 'reserve tokens of thinking, zero answer'). I ran the existing suite with the field unset and IT PASSED, so the current tests cannot see it. Flooring at the wire rather than trusting construction makes the bad state unrepresentable for any future struct-literal client, and means NO existing test had to be edited to accommodate this change.

Gemini carries the IDENTICAL hardcoded 2048 (generate(): `visibleBudget := 2048`) and the bug filing never mentioned it, because that session read only the Anthropic client. Fixing one provider and leaving the other is how this family keeps recurring — 016b §9's 'one call site of a shared judgement gets the rigorous fix, the sibling stays heuristic'. The configured value is the VISIBLE-text budget, so thinkingReserve is added on top of it exactly as it is for a caller-supplied budget; __sent_max_tokens keeps carrying the visible budget, preserving the cross-provider comparability bugs_open/110 established.

DELIBERATELY ASYMMETRIC, and this is the edit most worth arguing with. Ollama currently omits num_predict entirely when no budget is supplied, letting the server apply its own default. It therefore uses configMaxTokens (0 = 'nothing chosen') and NOT resolvedMaxTokens: this bug is about a CONFIGURED budget failing to arrive, and imposing a 2048 ceiling where there never was one would be a regression dressed as a fix. The default is applied before the options block and OUTSIDE the `if options != nil` guard, because a nil options map is precisely the case 257 is about.

Assertions against the request BODY, per prompt_caching_test's reason: a client that dropped the configured budget passes any response-only test while quietly truncating every reply. Clients are built through the REAL constructors with only the transport swapped, so config parsing and request building are covered together. Negative controls in the same run (unconfigured anthropic/gemini must still send 2048; unconfigured ollama must send NO num_predict), so a fix of 'always send N' fails. ELEVEN mutations run: M1-M8 and M11 were killed; M9 (accept max_tokens: 0 as configured) SURVIVED because the wire-level floor sits in SERIES with the resolver — so the 'unusable values' test was passing for the wrong reason. That is why configMaxTokens is now asserted DIRECTLY on its (int, bool) pair, which killed M9. M10 (delete the nil-config branch) is an EQUIVALENT mutant — Go returns the zero value for a nil-map read — and is documented as such in the source rather than left looking untested.

CANDIDATE 4 LIVES IN THIS SAME FILE. Candidate 4, at a layer that cannot be fooled by a comment. The bug proposed a source-scan lint over GenerateText call sites; this estate has been bitten by exactly that (register OPP-003: the first version gated on the FILE containing GenerateText, examined zero files, and printed a clean result — a clean result and an unrun check are byte-identical output). So the contract is bound BEHAVIOURALLY for the three implemented providers, and a source scan is used only to notice a provider that has no behavioural coverage: it reads factory.go's `case "x":` lines and fails if one both constructs successfully and is absent from the covered set. It also fails if the scan matches nothing, so it cannot pass for the wrong reason. Note this guards the PROVIDER axis, not the call-site axis — after this change a direct caller passing nil is no longer a defect, so there is nothing left to lint there.

This header states that an action bypassing ExecuteAIStepAction 'silently gets the provider's hardcoded fallback instead, whatever the config says'. THIS CHANGE MAKES THAT SENTENCE FALSE, and a false explanation sitting next to working code is how folklore starts. Corrected in place and dated, not deleted — the original was true when written and the record of the change is the useful part. The correction also says why the helper is STILL the right thing to call (it reads the STEP's config, which no constructor ever sees, and it forwards budget_tokens), so it is not misread as 'the helper is obsolete'. Its stale line references (anthropic.go:109, moved to :185 by the bugs_open/244 caching work) are replaced with the constant name, which will not rot.

grounded_in: bugs_open/257 §1 — "So the contract is: 'call through ExecuteAIStepAction, or your configuration is inert.' Nothing states that, nothing checks it, and the compiler is happy either way — GenerateText accepts nil."

bugs_open/257 §5 candidate 1 — "Resolve the budget inside the provider client (aiservice.NewClient already receives the whole ai_service config). If the client read max_tokens from the config it was constructed with, EVERY caller would inherit it, including nil-passing ones, and the defect class would stop being reachable. This is the only candidate that removes the choice rather than documenting it."
